title: Adventure, Scene, Encounter & Set-Piece Assembly
objective: Extend the MAS workspace by assembling prepared Adventure, Scene, Encounter and set-piece definitions through explicit references and proposals on top of MAS-01 workspace authority and MAS-02 structure, without duplicating canonical owner-domain state or treating prepared assembly as live run truth.

scope.purpose: Assemble prepared Adventure, Scene, Encounter and set-piece material inside the MAS authoring workspace while preserving existing object authorities and the prepared-definition/live-occurrence boundary.
scope.completion_gate: A representative MAS workspace can deterministically assemble prepared Adventure, Scene, Encounter and set-piece material through explicit references/proposals while preserving MAS-01/MAS-02 foundations, canonical owner authority and the boundary between prepared content and live occurrences.

selection_boundaries: MAS-01 workspace/document authority and MAS-02 higher-order structural organization remain foundational and were not reopened.
Adventure, Scene and Encounter owner domains remain canonical validation/state/mutation authorities; MAS-03 consumes explicit validated references and receipts only.
Set pieces are prepared MAS composition and do not create a new canonical owner domain.
Prepared assembly remains distinct from live run state and never proves an occurrence or canonical mutation.
MAS-04 route, choice, consequence and dependency-graph semantics were explicitly left unset by MAS-03.
Existing MAS validation family remained active; no family transition occurred in MAS-03.
ROADMAP_DEPENDENCY_GRAPH.json was reconsulted after MAS-03, including the new MSLR planning edges; no new cross-program rotation is unlocked at MAS-03, so MAS-04 is selected_not_started.
CNI-12 and PCA remain unselected; MAS-05+ and SMB-08 were not implemented by this tranche.
next_action: MAS-03 is closed. MAS-04 is selected_not_started after ROADMAP_DEPENDENCY_GRAPH reconciliation and requires a later owner Continue before governed start.
